subject: Food Science
title: High-Pressure Processing
description: A short lesson to help you apply High-Pressure Processing.

hook.text: Squeeze juice at 6,000 atmospheres—the pressure at the bottom of the deepest ocean—and bacteria explode. The juice stays fresh.

buildup.text: High-pressure processing (HPP) uses extreme pressure to destroy microbes without heat, preserving flavor and nutrients.

discovery.text: HPP-treated guacamole stays green for 30 days. Without it, avocado browns within hours.

twist.text: HPP doesn't kill bacterial spores. It complements but can't replace thermal processing for low-acid canned foods.

climax.text: Cold-pressed juice brands like Suja use HPP instead of pasteurization—keeping the 'raw' label while ensuring safety.

punchline.text: No heat, no flavor loss. Just 6,000 atmospheres of crushing pressure.

quiz.question: What does high-pressure processing do to bacteria?
options: Destroys them with extreme pressure without heat
